newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees progress on power privatizations.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees progress on power privatizations.

text.p: At least six state-level Brazilian power utilities are close to privatization and progress is being made on the selloff of federal generating companies due to begin in 1997, a senior power official said.
Fermino Sampaio, president of federal power holding Eletrobras, said Coelba, a power company belonging to Bahia state, would be privatized by July.
A further five state-level companies were "virtually ready for sale," Sampaio said.
Those five were Cemat (Mato Grosso state), Enersul (Rio Grando do Sul), Coserne (Rio Grande do Norte), Ceal (Alagoas) and Energipe (Sergipe).

Eletrobras and the National Development Bank (BNDES) helped the states prepare their utilities for privatization and in January signed similar agreements with the states of Piaui and Rondonia, which plan to sell their power companies.
The government expects 70 percent of Brazil's power distribution to be in private hands by the end of 1998.
Rio de Janeiro last year sold its power utility Cerj and giant Sao Paulo state is shortly due to appoint constulants to advise on the privatization of Eletropaulo, CPFL and CESP.
Sampaio, speaking at a seminar on the restructuring of Brazil's power industry, said he expected federal generators Furnas and CHESF to be divided up into smaller units for privatization.
By selling the two big generators in several blocks, the government would improve competition in the industry, find it easier to attract investors and generate more revenues, he said.

The government hopes to sell Furnas and the smaller Eletrosul in 1997 -- the BNDES is currently hiring consultants for those selloffs -- followed by CHESF and Eletronorte in 1998, completing privatization of the generating sector.

Sampaio also said studies had begun for the privatization of two independent power systems in the Amazon region, one in and around the city of Manaus, capital of Amazonas state, the other in Boa Vista, Roraima state.
He said those two systems will be sold complete with their transmission assets.
Elsewhere, the government intends to maintain control over transmission to ensure free access to the grid during a first phase after privatization of the generators.
